title: KV cache 'prefetch floaters' memory-growth postmortem and mitigation roadmap
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2025-02-08 03:14 UTC we observed sustained memory growth on a subset of KV-cache serving shards in us-west-2, leading to OOM restarts and increased tail latency for text generation requests. The immediate remediation (2025-02-08 04:02) was to scale up the affected node pool and enable a conservative eviction throttle. This stopped OOMs but did not address the root cause.

Impact:
- 6% of hosted inference requests experienced elevated latency during the event window.
- 3 GPU workers in us-west-2 restarted due to OOM between 03:20–04:05 UTC.
- No customer data exfiltration; requests were served with best-effort fallbacks.

Detection and timeline:
- 2025-02-08 02:58 UTC: internal memory anomaly alert (per-shard heap growth).
- 2025-02-08 03:14 UTC: alert escalated as OOMs started.
- 2025-02-08 03:40 UTC: triage call; mitigation applied (temporary eviction throttle + scale-up).
- 2025-02-08 08:30 UTC: initial postmortem triage completed.

Root cause (summary):
Concurrent prefetch + eviction race that allowed "floating" prefetched entries to be re-inserted into slabs after their eviction tombstone epoch had advanced. The prefetch path did not validate the tombstone epoch atomically with insertion, so the following sequence could happen under load:
  1) Evictor removes an entry and advances the shard tombstone epoch.
  2) Asynchronous prefetcher (running on per-shard worker) observes the key missing and schedules an async load.
  3) Before prefetch completes, a concurrent read or eviction path advances metadata such that the prefetch's completion callback performs an insert that bypasses the tombstone check, creating an entry whose internal refcount was inconsistent with the slab allocator's accounting.
  4) That entry becomes unreachable from the normal index paths (because higher-priority tombstone metadata was applied), but still holds slab allocations -> "floating" entries that are not reclaimed byusual eviction or compact paths. Over many such races, memory accumulates leading to OOM.

Why this escaped earlier tests:
- Unit tests exercised insert/evict paths but did not simulate the specific async-finish-after-tombstone interleaving at scale.
- The prefetch logic was recently optimized for latency and bypassed a defensive tombstone check that had been present in the old codepath.

Mitigation applied during incident:
- Re-enabled a temporary tombstone validation in the prefetch completion path (hotfix cf. PR #12345) to prevent re-inserting after tombstone epoch advancement. Deployed as a narrow canary to us-west-2.
- Enabled conservative eviction throttle to slow churn while we investigated.

Permanent fixes proposed and prioritized in this ticket (see Action Items):
- Correct atomic insert semantics for asynchronous prefetch completion: insert-if-not-present must check tombstone epoch and fail cleanly, decrementing any temporary refcount before returning.
- Add a background compaction sweep that detects and reclaims floating entries by cross-checking slab allocations against the index map. This is a safety net for pre-existing floating entries and will run opportunistically during low-traffic windows.
- Strengthen telemetry: per-shard gauge 'kvcache.floating_entries' and counter 'kvcache.prefetch_reinsert_fail' with alert thresholds.
- Add a race-injection test harness to the kvcache integration test suite that can deterministically reproduce the prefetch-after-tombstone interleaving.
- Update runbook: new playbook steps for identifying floating-entry growth, and a rapid remediation for future incidents (enable compaction sweep + throttle prefetchers).

Decision rationale and trade-offs:
- We prefer adding a lightweight compaction sweep as a safety net rather than immediate heavy-handed slab rebalancing because compaction is low-risk and can run with CPU throttles during off-peak windows.
- The atomic insert fix is prioritized over aggressive eviction because it addresses the root cause; however, we will keep eviction throttle gates as a short-term operational lever.

Open questions (to resolve before close):
- Should prefetched entries carry a short-lived provisional TTL that triggers automatic reclamation if they never become linked? (Pros: bounds memory growth; Cons: may reduce cache hit-rate for legitimate prefetches).
- Can we opportunistically piggyback reclamation on existing lazy-compact paths to avoid new background work?

Next steps (high level):
1) Implementation + tests (owner: Marco Diaz) — due 2025-02-18.
2) Safety-net compaction (owner: Priya Nair) — due 2025-02-25.
3) Telemetry + alerting (owner: SRE team, contact: Jordan Lee) — due 2025-02-20.
4) Canary rollout and monitoring (owner: Marco Diaz) — start 2025-02-19, canary 24h, then ramp.

Notes on observability:
- Dashboard: kvcache/us-west-2/heap-growth (internal) — used to detect event.
- Existing alerts were noisy for eviction churn and suppressed the early signal; we will refine alert thresholds after telemetry is added.

Longer-term ideas (parking lot):
- Rework prefetcher to use coordinated per-key leases to avoid concurrent repaired re-inserts.
- Consider per-tenant slab quotas to limit blast radius of leaks.
action_items: ENG: Implement atomic prefetch completion insert-if-not-present with tombstone epoch check and proper refcount decrement (owner: Marco Diaz) — due 2025-02-18
ENG: Add background compaction sweep to detect/reclaim floating slab allocations (owner: Priya Nair) — due 2025-02-25
SRE: Add telemetry and alerts: kvcache.floating_entries (gauge), kvcache.prefetch_reinsert_fail (counter) and update alert thresholds (owner: Jordan Lee) — due 2025-02-20
ENG: Add race-injection test harness in integration suite and fuzz test for prefetch/evict interleave (owner: Marco Diaz) — due 2025-02-18
ENG: Update runbook with detection steps and emergency compaction procedure (owner: Aisha Patel) — due 2025-02-21
OPS: Canary rollout coordination and post-canary review (owner: Release Eng) — start 2025-02-19
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit + integration tests that reproducibly exercise the prefetch-after-tombstone race pass in CI. 2) Canary deployment shows no increase in floating_entries gauge and no memory growth over 24h under production-like load. 3) New telemetry emitted and alerts validated. 4) Compaction sweep runs and reclaims pre-existing floating entries in a controlled test environment.
implementation_notes:
- Key change: use compare-and-insert against shard tombstone epoch atomically; if insert would violate epoch, fail and ensure any temporary allocations are freed before return.
- Add guard to prefetch completion path to never directly manipulate slab refcounts without acquiring per-shard insert lock on shadow path.
- Compaction will be implemented as an idempotent background job with a low CPU budget and dry-run mode for first rollout.
- Add metrics for durations and counts of prefetched keys, failed reinserts, and reclaimed entries.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR behind feature flag. 2) Run full CI + race-injection suite. 3) Canary to 10% of us-west-2 kvcache shards for 24h with enhanced telemetry. 4) If green, ramp to remaining us-west-2 shards over 6h. 5) Global roll after 48h observation window. Rollback plan: flip feature flag off and trigger compaction sweep to reclaim any floating entries produced by canary. Rollout owner: Marco Diaz.
tests: Unit tests for atomic insert and tombstone validation
Integration race harness that deterministically reproduces prefetch-after-tombstone interleaving
Load test with synthetic prefetch traffic and eviction churn in staging to validate no memory growth
Post-deploy e2e smoke that verifies reclamation counts and no regression in hit rates
